prior_items.title: ASIC proposes bringing crypto-settled derivative contracts under CFD leverage rules, with public consultation closing November 9; captured Morgan Stanley tokenization headline has no supporting text
prior_items.summary:
A Lookonchain feed digest captured under the headline 'Morgan Stanley Executive: Tokenized RWA Market to Reach $3 Trillion to $10 Trillion by the 2030s' contains no text about Morgan Stanley or any tokenized real-world-asset projection; what the capture holds is a six-item policy and market roundup, so that headline claim rests on the title alone.

According to the capture, Australia's Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) proposed on a Monday to expand the regulatory scope of Contracts for Difference (CFDs) to include contracts that meet relevant conditions and settle via digital asset transfers, with contracts potentially covered even where they track non-crypto asset prices, while certain cryptocurrency futures and options with fixed expiration dates would remain excluded from CFD rules. The item describes the existing CFD framework as imposing leverage caps, requiring providers to close positions when a client's account funds fall below a required threshold, and mandating negative balance protection that limits client losses to the funds in their CFD trading accounts. It states that public consultation on the proposal closes on November 9, and adds as separate background that Australia passed legislation in April this year requiring cryptocurrency exchanges and tokenized custody platforms to be included in the financial services licensing framework, with that regime set to take effect on April 9, 2027.

On market flows, the digest relays a post by crypto market analyst Axel Adler Jr stating that last week the market absorbed selling pressure of 220,374 BTC while net exchange flow stood at -3,863 BTC — more Bitcoin leaving exchanges than entering — which the capture frames as reflecting relatively strong buying demand. A companion item reports that Strategy added 249 BTC last week, taking its total holdings to 848,250 coins, while its US dollar reserves fell to $5.52 billion, a $193 million drop.

Another item relays an Arkham post stating that the analytics platform has labeled wallets under Justin Sun's name across 10 blockchains holding roughly $2.25 billion in on-chain assets, and that its September ranking places Sun second only to Satoshi Nakamoto, whose holdings it puts at $91.3 billion; the capture describes Sun as founder of TRON, CEO of BitTorrent, and owner of two cryptocurrency exchanges.

On French policy, the capture reports that the National Assembly's Finance Committee passed multiple crypto tax amendments last week. These would add crypto assets such as Bitcoin — covering assets held on overseas platforms and in personal self-custody wallets — to the exit tax that currently applies to taxpayers who lived in France for at least six of the past ten years and hold over €800,000 in stocks and other securities when leaving the country, starting in 2027, and would impose a maximum €10,000 fine on unreported large-value self-custody wallets. Per the capture, tax rates are not yet specified; some taxpayers relocating to the EU or specific countries could defer payment and, if they retain assets for a required 2-to-5-year period, have the tax canceled; taxpayers with €100,000 or more in self-custody wallet assets at year-end would be required to file voluntary reports; conversions of crypto to stablecoins would be taxed from 2027; crypto losses could offset gains over the next 10 years; and the fine for failing to submit documents to tax authorities would rise from €10,000 to €50,000 per instance. None of the measures is officially effective: the committee rejected the revenue section of the 2027 budget bill, so the amendments must be reintroduced and voted on by the full National Assembly, with votes expected on October 20 for the revenue part and November 17 for the full bill.

A market item states that Bitcoin kicked off the week above $83,000, down roughly 0.5% alongside gold near $4,180 per ounce, as a stronger US dollar and rising US Treasury yields set a cautious tone, with the Dollar Index above 102.4, tech stock futures slightly lower, and WTI crude above $92 per barrel. It points to US inflation data due Wednesday — with markets expecting core CPI up 2.5% year-over-year and headline CPI up 3.7% — as the week's key focus, noting that in-line figures would mark a reacceleration from the prior month and could further shape views on Federal Reserve policy. The same item, attributing the report to The Information, relays that IREN, having shifted from Bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure operations, struck a multi-year cloud services deal with AI firm Anthropic, after which IREN's US pre-market shares rose roughly 4%.

prior_items.title: Bitdeer sets January 2027 start for 901 capacity delivery and 67 MW target by Q2 2027
prior_items.summary:
Bitdeer Technologies Group has laid out a delivery schedule for its next data center build-out, saying it plans to begin delivering capacity for its 901 site in January 2027 and to reach 67 MW by the second quarter of that year. The Singapore-based company, which trades on Nasdaq under BTDR, has been stacking up capacity commitments for its AI Cloud and high-performance computing business, much of it in Malaysia.

The 901 schedule sits alongside the company's A201 data center in Johor Bahru, which carries roughly 21.7 MW of IT capacity. Bitdeer states that off-take commitments cover more than 70% of A201, that the facility is expected to energize in the first quarter of 2027, and that the contracted capacity is expected to generate more than $1.7 billion in revenue over five years. Next door, the A202 site adds 65.1 MW and targets energization in the third quarter of 2027 under a 10-year agreement, bringing the Johor Bahru campus to a planned 86.8 MW. The smaller A102 site, at 9.5 MW, is fully contracted and expected to contribute more than $800 million.

Following the A201 commitments, Bitdeer puts its expected AI Cloud revenue backlog at around $2.9 billion. The company maintains a target of up to 350 MW of AI Cloud capacity by the first quarter of 2028, with recent announcements bringing secured capacity to approximately 333.5 MW. Per the article, the 350 MW plan is financed largely through customer prepayments and contractual financing, meaning clients effectively help fund the facilities they will use.

Bitdeer continues to operate as a vertically integrated Bitcoin mining company with operations in several countries, and says it can allocate electricity flexibly between mining and AI services using infrastructure originally built for Bitcoin. It has also been designated a preferred NVIDIA Cloud Partner, and between September and October 2026 it pushed forward on GPU procurement and signed incremental site agreements.

The article frames the January 2027 start, the Q2 2027 ramp, and the A201 and A202 energization dates as plans rather than completed milestones. It notes that a meaningful share of the contracted capacity sits on a single Malaysian campus, so local permitting, power supply, or policy changes could ripple through several projects at once, and identifies the near-term checkpoints as the 901 delivery start in January 2027, A201's Q1 2027 energization, and whether the gap between roughly 333.5 MW secured and the 350 MW goal closes before Q1 2028.

prior_items.title: After Proposal 613's cancellation, a Compound forum proposal would move EPCF and SVR custody from Foundation-controlled Safes to the Community Multisig
prior_items.summary: Compound forum user ugurmersin posted a proposal outline on comp.xyz on October 8, 2026, one day after the Proposal Guardian cancelled Proposal 613 on October 7. The alternative would leave the EPCF (Ecosystem Protection and Continuity Fund) open but change who holds the keys: per the post, the EPCF's holdings — 500,000 USDC plus 4,583,411 USDC supplied to cUSDCv3 — and the mainnet Chainlink SVR revenue of 355.95 ETH would move from Safes the Compound Foundation controls alone to the Community Multisig, which acts by five-of-nine signer approval. The author says the EPCF would keep its purposes, size and 48-month term, with emergency deployment still available, distinguishing the plan from Proposal 613, which he writes would have closed the fund and sent everything to the Governor Timelock over objections including pennblockchain's that this removed the fund's rapid-response role. Arguing that DAO funds elsewhere sit behind a committee, a withdrawal cooldown and reclamation paths while these two pools do not, the author notes both Safes are controlled by the same two addresses. As context for why custody matters now, he recounts on-chain activity around the V2 reserves granted under Proposal 536 — including COMP arrivals close to governance voting snapshots, a 912,717 COMP vote for Proposal 580, transfers routed through wallets to eight exchanges, and USDT returned to the Safe — which he characterizes as misappropriation. The Foundation disputes that characterization and stated in a September 28 forum post that there has been no trading; the author concedes exchange-internal trades are not visible on-chain and asks the Foundation to publish its trading-firm agreement and transfer records. He argues the Community Multisig, nine organizations that already hold the DAO's Pause Guardian, Treasury Escrow Safeguard and Proposal Guardian roles, is a stronger check than two signers from one organization, while saying he still views its composition as imperfect and the proposal as the minimum rather than the ideal.

prior_items.title: Compound DAO considers extending treasury safeguards under heightened oversight
prior_items.summary: Compound DAO is voting on Proposal 612, submitted by Ugur Mersin, which would extend the Treasury Escrow withdrawal cooldown and Treasury Timelock minimum delay from two days to ten. The proposal would also give the Governor Timelock authority to execute or cancel Treasury Timelock actions and set a 17-day Escrow expiration, leaving a seven-day withdrawal window after the cooldown. Voting opened October 4, 2026, and was scheduled to end October 7. A wallet linked to delegate Humpy had cast 1.75 million COMP in favor, while 921,000 COMP opposed the measure, according to Crypto Briefing. The proposal follows recent Treasury Management Committee activity, including a September 29 transfer of $3 million in stablecoins and a $2 million USDC deployment into a Uniswap V3 COMP position. The article also referenced allegations that the Compound Foundation exchanged 8.42 million DAI for about 344,780 COMP before important governance votes, while noting that the claims had not been established as findings.

prior_items.title: HIVE Digital Technologies plans Phase 3 expansion to 400 MW at Paraguay hydro campus
prior_items.summary:
HIVE Digital Technologies is adding another 100 MW to its hydroelectric data center campus in Yguazú, Paraguay — a Phase 3 build that would bring the site's total capacity to 400 MW, all of it drawn from the Itaipú Dam. The company is targeting completion by Q3 2026, and states that if the schedule holds, the campus would become the largest hydro-powered facility in Paraguay.

The build continues a staged rollout: HIVE bought the Yguazú data center from Bitfarms in January 2025, brought Phase 1 online in April 2025 at 200 MW, and followed with Phase 2 in September 2025, lifting the site to 300 MW. At its current size, the campus produces approximately 8.5 BTC per day, per company reporting. Since the acquisition, HIVE says it has committed more than $400 million to its Paraguay operations, with $130 million of that toward construction costs and the remainder covering taxes and other buildout.

The added capacity feeds into a broader company target: HIVE aims to reach 35 exahashes per second of global Bitcoin mining capacity by the end of 2026, up from 22 EH/s as of October 2025.

Bitcoin is only part of the Paraguay plan. The company also intends to build out high-performance computing and AI infrastructure, planning a dedicated AI factory powered by a new 100 MW substation that it anticipates will come online in the second half of 2027, alongside a stated goal of scaling its HPC and AI capabilities fivefold.

HIVE, which trades on the TSX Venture Exchange and Nasdaq under the ticker HIVE, points to the Itaipú Dam's hydroelectric abundance as Paraguay's appeal, letting it lock in competitive energy rates in an industry where electricity is often the biggest operating cost. The company also participates in demand response, adjusting its power usage with grid needs. Gabriel Lamas, HIVE's Country President in Paraguay, has framed the company as a contributor to the nation's energy resilience, arguing that its ability to modulate demand helps stabilize the grid rather than simply drain it.

The article frames Phase 3 as the test of whether HIVE's 2025 execution pace holds, flags concentration risk in placing a large share of growth in a single country and a single power source, and points to the Q3 2026 completion target, changes in daily Bitcoin output once the new capacity is live, and the 2027 AI factory timeline as milestones to watch.

prior_items.title: Hyperscale Data's Ault Markets opens live, invite-only access to beta DEX on Ault Blockchain
prior_items.summary: Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS) said in an Oct. 8, 2026 press release that Ault Markets is now providing live, invite-only access to the decentralized exchange (DEX) currently operating in beta format on the Ault Blockchain. Per the release, Ault Markets, Inc. created the Ault Markets software to provide access to the DEX, which launched natively on the Ault Blockchain, and — following the model of other decentralized exchanges — listing decisions and trading on the exchange are not controlled by a centralized entity. The company framed the launch as following its previously announced plans to develop the exchange and expand its blockchain-based financial technology offerings. Access remains by invitation only: interested participants can visit AultMarkets.com to request an invitation and join a list for updates on new assets and platform developments. Hyperscale Data said it plans to substantially expand the range of assets available on Ault Markets and tradeable on the DEX, with planned additions including tokenized silver, tokenized gold and tokenized platinum, and that further announcements will provide details as those products progress toward launch. Executive Chairman Milton 'Todd' Ault III said the company had been developing Ault Markets 'for some time' and had shared its progress 'through a series of press releases over the past year and a half,' adding, 'The platform we have been discussing is now live, and we are very proud of the work that our team and our core contributors accomplished to reach this milestone.' He also said the company believes tokenization will be one of the most important developments in financial markets over the next 10 years, with the potential to change how people access, own and trade assets, and that the company is proud to have Ault Markets positioned to participate in that opportunity. The company said it will continue to update stockholders and interested participants as the invitation-only rollout progresses and additional assets are introduced. The release did not state when the access went live, which assets are currently listed on the beta DEX, or when the planned tokenized metals could launch, and it included no figures on users or trading activity.

prior_items.title: Hyperscale Data reaffirms 2027 outlook and schedules Nov. 12 Investor Day centered on potential Michigan campus sale
prior_items.summary: Hyperscale Data (AMEX: GPUS) reaffirmed its 2027 outlook and scheduled a Nov. 12 Investor Day at which it plans to detail the potential sale of its Michigan campus. The company is targeting $300 million to $350 million in 2027 revenue and $60 million to $80 million in adjusted EBITDA, and it previously estimated the campus could be worth $750 million to $1.25 billion. At the event, management plans to update investors on an agreement with a California-based neocloud provider covering an initial 20 MW of AI compute capacity targeted to launch in November 2026, with options to expand to 52 MW — a deployment the company projects could generate more than $3 billion in revenue over 20 years. Hyperscale Data, which says it has already invested more than $70 million in subsidiary Alliance Cloud Services and the Michigan site, estimates the campus could ultimately support over 300 MW, depending on financing, approvals, infrastructure, and demand. Management also said it will likely discuss strategic options for two subsidiaries, Sentinum, Inc. and askROI, Inc. Separately, the company has previously announced plans to move its Bitcoin mining operations into Patriot BTC, splitting them from its Michigan and Montana data centers so the Michigan campus can focus on AI compute. The Investor Day agenda also covers Hyperscale's defense, energy, real estate, finance, and technology businesses, plus blockchain initiatives at Ault Markets, Inc. Executive Chairman Milton "Todd" Ault III said, "We are focused on delivering the contracted capacity in our Michigan Campus and turning that investment into cash flow." At the time of publication on Monday, Hyperscale Data shares were up 1.80% at $0.17, according to Benzinga Pro data.

prior_items.title: Hyperscale Data shuts down Michigan Bitcoin mining to convert the site into an AI data center
prior_items.summary:
Per a September 3 report by PANews, citing Cointelegraph, Hyperscale Data has shut down its Bitcoin mining operations at its Michigan facility in order to convert the site into an AI data center. The company said all miners at the site have been powered off and that it plans to sell the related mining equipment.

The company stated that a customer has signed a contract for 20 megawatts of AI computing capacity at the facility over a 10-year term that includes two five-year renewal options. Per the report, the contract is expected to generate more than $1.2 billion in revenue over 20 years, and an additional 32-megawatt option could push potential revenue above $3 billion. These figures are presented as company projections and are not independently verified in the report, which does not identify the customer.

The report says Hyperscale is financing the transition by selling its Bitcoin holdings: per the article, the company's holdings fell from about 1,006 BTC at the end of July to 215 BTC, a decline of about 79% that dropped it to 84th among publicly traded companies ranked by Bitcoin holdings. The article does not state at what prices the holdings were sold or how much the sales raised.

Per the report, Hyperscale Data's stock fell about 17% on Wednesday to $0.1984, which the article describes as a new all-time low on a split-adjusted basis. The article gives no specific timestamps for the shutdown, the contract signing, or the Bitcoin sales, and anchors the share-price decline only to an unnamed Wednesday.

prior_items.title: Mykhailo Fedorov pushes for AI on Ukraine's battlefields
prior_items.summary:
Mykhailo Fedorov, dismissed as Ukraine's defense minister in July 2026, has continued arguing publicly about how Ukraine should fight, and his current case is that the country should put artificial intelligence on the front lines against Russia now. In an interview dated October 7, 2026, the former minister said Ukraine must deploy AI on the battlefield "without delay," framing AI-powered robots as a matter of survival and a way to keep Ukrainian soldiers alive in a war he described as increasingly fought by machines.

Making the case for machines over manpower, Fedorov pointed to drones as proof the model already works. He said Ukrainian drones account for 95% of Russian casualties, while separate findings described in the article attribute over 95% of strikes against Russian forces to drones. He also noted that more than 700 Ukrainian UAV manufacturers are currently operating, supplying hardware to the front.

Fedorov's push lines up with the "Army of Robots" initiative announced on September 26, 2026. The program aims to deploy humanoid robots and enable autonomous assault operations within a year, with a stated target of achieving the first humanoid kill within six months.

Since leaving government, Fedorov has shifted to the private side of defense. His plans include a defense tech investment vehicle, and the article reports he has drawn backing from Palantir CEO Alex Karp.

The article frames the stakes for Ukraine's military around manpower: if AI-powered robots can take on dangerous missions, fewer soldiers face the front-line risks that have defined the war. It also flags risks to watch — autonomous weapons remain one of the most debated topics in modern warfare, and goals like a "first humanoid kill" within six months will draw scrutiny over how much decision-making is handed to machines. Concrete markers ahead include whether the initiative hits its six-month humanoid target and one-year autonomous assault goal, and whether Fedorov's investment vehicle launches and which companies it funds.

prior_items.title: After the CPI release, U.S. stocks decline across semiconductor, storage, optical communication and crypto-related sectors, with optical communication leading losses; separate briefs cover USDC's EU designation, an OpenAI leak accusation, Ondo's $4B TVL and a whale's $8.93M ETH profit
prior_items.summary:
A Lookonchain feed page published on October 14, 2026 reports, citing BIT (bit.com) market data, that U.S. stocks slumped during U.S. stock trading hours, with the page's headline framing the pressure as following the release of U.S. CPI data. Per the market brief, the S&P 500's decline widened to 1.1%, the Nasdaq fell 1.64%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3%. The brief says semiconductor, storage, optical communication, and crypto-related stocks all fell across the board, with optical communication leading losses as most major stocks in the sector declined by more than 7%. In semiconductor and storage, it lists Seagate down 2.8%, Western Digital down 3.2%, SanDisk down 4.7%, Micron down 3.3%, NVIDIA down 2.9%, Intel down 4.2%, and AMD down 5.3%. Among crypto-related stocks, it lists Strategy down 5.8%, Coinbase down 4.6%, Circle down 6.4%, BitMine Immersion down 5.3%, and SharpLink Gaming down 7.4%. In optical communication, it lists the Pure Photonics ETF (FOTO) down 6.2%, Marvell down 5.8%, Applied Optoelectronics down 9.8%, Lumentum down 7.2%, Coherent down 7.8%, and Ciena down 7.8%. The market brief itself names no cause for the declines; the CPI tie appears in the page's headline and, as described below, in one whale item's framing.

In a separate brief, the European Banking Authority (EBA) announced it has classified USDC, issued by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS, as an Important Electronic Money Token under the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation — per the item, the first of the 45 EMTs that have completed notification under MiCA to receive that designation, which the page's headline summarizes as 'systemically important.' Per the item, starting November 12, 2026 USDC will be subject to dual supervision: direct regulatory responsibilities for own funds, asset reserves, liquidity requirements, and recovery and redemption plans transfer from the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) to the EBA, while ACPR retains oversight of governance, qualifying holdings, suitability assessments, outsourcing, and conflicts of interest. The item adds that USDC is issued in the EU by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS and in the U.S. by Circle Internet Financial, LLC, and that the EBA has signed a memorandum of understanding with the New York State Department of Financial Services to facilitate cooperation and information exchange on cross-border stablecoin activities.

Citing Reuters, the page reports that OpenAI has accused a former employee of sending more than 100 files related to its unreleased devices to a personal account before leaving to join Apple, and of later presenting the relevant products to Apple's senior management. Per the item, Apple had earlier filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging theft of trade secrets covering unreleased hardware products, in what both versions of the item — the feed runs the story twice in near-identical form — describe as a further escalation of the intellectual property dispute between the two companies over hardware technology.

The page also relays an Ondo Finance announcement that the total value locked across its tokenized products stands at $4 billion, with tokenized stocks and ETFs exceeding $1.3 billion, that it holds the leading position in the tokenized U.S. Treasuries segment, and that cumulative holders of its products have surpassed 1 million. Per the item, its tokens can be permissionlessly transferred across networks including Solana, Ethereum, and BNB Chain, and Ondo Stocks accesses traditional financial liquidity through a request-for-quote (RFQ) mechanism.

Finally, per EmberCN's on-chain monitoring as relayed, after a market drop that the item attributes to the release of U.S. CPI data and describes as occurring 'tonight,' a whale that opened a 20,000 ETH long position at $1,936 at the very start of the rally on August 19 closed the position 'today,' two months later, at $2,421.6, locking in a profit of $8.93 million. The item notes that when ETH reached $2,800 on September 22 the position's unrealized profit peaked at $17.42 million, making the realized gain roughly half that peak.

Across the page, the briefs — each stamped only with a relative '14 minutes ago' timestamp — stand side by side with no stated connection drawn between the market report and the other items, and no absolute clock times are given for any of the events described. All figures, percentages and claims are relayed as presented by the page and the sources it cites, without independent verification.

prior_items.title: Matter Labs open-sources Prividium permissioning engine; Deutsche Bundesbank tests self-hosted instance
prior_items.summary:
Matter Labs, the company behind the ZKsync protocol, made the core permissioning engine of its Prividium enterprise blockchain platform publicly available on September 8, 2026, releasing the code under the Apache 2.0 license. According to the publication's report, the release covers one main application and six packages in a public GitHub repository, matter-labs/prividium-core.

Germany's Deutsche Bundesbank is the first organization testing a self-hosted instance of Prividium, the report states, and is collaborating with Matter Labs on both design and testing for its deployment. The report presents this as a test rather than a production rollout.

The permissioning engine is the component that decides who can do what on a private chain — a layer the publication says carries particular weight for regulated institutions, where permissions and auditability are central compliance concerns. Its release completes a stack whose other pieces — ZKsync OS, the Atlas sequencer, the Airbender prover, and the interoperability contracts — had already been open-sourced. With the engine public, the report says institutions can now independently build permissioned chains using publicly shared code; previously, the gatekeeping layer was the missing piece of the publicly available stack.

Under the Apache 2.0 license, the report notes, institutions can inspect and modify the engine without signing a commercial agreement for that specific component — a bank can read every line, change what it needs, and run it in-house without needing Matter Labs' permission.

The release is not total. Matter Labs is keeping its enterprise tooling — user interfaces and deployment tools — proprietary, an arrangement the publication characterizes as giving away the engine while selling the car built around it.

Matter Labs framed the open-source move as a response to institutional feedback, saying large organizations had voiced wariness about depending on a single vendor for critical technology, per the report. Prividium is built for validium-style chains in which transaction data stays off-chain for privacy while the chain anchors to Ethereum through zero-knowledge proofs; the publication notes that institutional adoption of this model would route more enterprise activity back to Ethereum as the settlement layer.

The report also points to the limits of the open engine on its own: institutions that self-host still need the skills to run and maintain the stack, which the proprietary deployment tools exist to address.
